chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the man to cleanse himself with his right hand.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using the right hand for istinja (cleansing after urination/defecation) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the legal ruling (hukm) of using the left hand for istinja, a practice rooted in the Sunnah to distinguish the right hand for honorable acts and the left for impure ones. In Shia jurisprudence, this prohibition is often understood as a recommendation (mustahabb) or a strong precaution (ihtiyat) to maintain ritual purity and bodily dignity, reflecting the Prophet's emphasis on cleanliness as part of faith. The narration, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni, underscores the continuity of prophetic guidance in daily hygiene practices.
